step: Employer applies for GEP employment visa on behalf of incoming employee
deadline_label: Apply at least 6 weeks before intended start date (processing 4–8 weeks)
non_obvious_official_guidance: A person may only work in Hong Kong if they hold a valid visa or entry permit expressly permitting employment with the named employer.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The employer — not the employee — files the GEP application; the employee cannot self-sponsor under this scheme. Standard processing is 4–8 weeks; the employee must not enter HK for work purposes until written approval is received and the visa label is affixed.
non_obvious_action_required: Employer must submit a genuine-vacancy justification, proposed salary, and evidence that the role cannot be filled locally. Do not allow employee to commence any work activity — including remote work from Hong Kong on a visitor entry — until approval is in hand.
source: Hong Kong Immigration Department – General Employment Policy

step: Employer applies under the Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals (ASMTP)
deadline_label: Apply at least 6 weeks before intended start date
non_obvious_official_guidance: ASMTP is specifically for mainland Chinese nationals; it operates without a quota but still requires employer sponsorship and a genuine vacancy.
non_obvious_actual_reality: ASMTP is quota-free but is not faster by default; the employer must still demonstrate the vacancy cannot be filled by a local HK resident. A mainland Chinese national cannot switch to GEP mid-process; the correct scheme must be selected from the outset.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm the employee holds a mainland Chinese travel document before selecting ASMTP over GEP. Submit with employment contract, proof of qualifications, and the employer's business registration certificate.
source: Hong Kong Immigration Department – Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals

step: Employee self-applies for Top Talent Pass Scheme (TTPS) visa
field_label: Top Talent Pass Scheme – Individual Application
deadline_label: Apply at least 4 weeks before intended arrival; no employer required for Categories A and B
non_obvious_official_guidance: TTPS allows eligible high-income or high-qualification individuals to enter Hong Kong for up to 2 years to explore opportunities; employment is permitted upon approval.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Unlike GEP/ASMTP, Categories A and B of TTPS do not require a job offer or employer sponsorship. The initial 2-year pass is self-sponsored. The employee may work for any employer in HK; they are not tied to the sponsoring company. Extension requires demonstrating ongoing employment or a business.
non_obvious_action_required: Check eligibility: Category A requires annual income ≥ HKD 2.5 million in the preceding year; Category B requires a degree from a top-100 global university plus 3 years' work experience. Category C requires a degree from a top-100 university with less experience but needs an employer offer. Submit supporting documents for the correct category.
source: Hong Kong Immigration Department – Top Talent Pass Scheme

step: Confirm employee performs no work in Hong Kong before visa is formally granted
field_label: No Work Before Visa Grant – Compliance Confirmation
deadline_label: Applies from date employee arrives until visa label is affixed
non_obvious_official_guidance: Working in Hong Kong without a valid visa or entry permit is an offence under the Immigration Ordinance (Cap. 115) and may result in prosecution and deportation.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Even attending a single client meeting, joining a video call from a HK address, or accessing company systems for business purposes while in HK on a visitor stamp before approval may constitute illegal employment. This applies even if the visa application is already submitted and pending.
non_obvious_action_required: Do not allow the employee to travel to HK for any work-related purpose until the approval letter has been issued and the visa label affixed. If a business trip is genuinely necessary before the visa is granted, obtain separate legal advice on what visitor activity is permissible.
source: Immigration Ordinance (Cap. 115) – Hong Kong Immigration Department

step: Employer or employee applies for dependant visa for accompanying spouse and minor children
field_label: Dependant Visa – Application for Spouse / Minor Children
deadline_label: Apply concurrently with or shortly after main employment visa application
non_obvious_official_guidance: Dependants are admitted on condition that they are wholly or mainly dependent on the principal visa holder; they may not work without obtaining a separate employment visa.
non_obvious_actual_reality: A dependant who takes any paid employment — including freelance or part-time work — without their own separate work visa is in breach of their conditions of stay. Dependant status is tied to the principal's continued employment visa; if the principal's visa lapses or the principal leaves HK, dependants' status lapses too.
non_obvious_action_required: Advise the spouse specifically that a dependant visa does not permit work. If the spouse intends to work in HK, a separate GEP or TTPS application must be filed. Keep principal visa renewal timelines aligned with dependant visa renewals.
source: Hong Kong Immigration Department – Dependant Visa

step: Employee presents approval letter at port of entry and receives visa label affixed to passport
field_label: Entry Visa Label – Port of Entry Collection
non_obvious_official_guidance: The approval letter for a pre-approved visa must be presented to the Immigration Officer at the port of entry, who will affix the visa label to the passport.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The approval letter is not the visa; work cannot commence until the label is physically affixed. The label specifies: permitted employer (GEP/ASMTP), permitted period of stay, and conditions. The employee should verify the employer name and expiry date at the immigration counter before leaving the airport.
non_obvious_action_required: Employee must carry the original approval letter (not a copy) to the port of entry. Check the conditions of stay on the label immediately; an error in the employer name must be corrected before the employee leaves immigration.
source: Hong Kong Immigration Department – Employment Visa

step: Book HKID card registration appointment at a Registration of Persons Office
authority: Immigration Department – Registration of Persons Office
deadline_label: Book within first week of arrival to secure a slot before the 30-day deadline
non_obvious_official_guidance: Any person who is 11 years of age or above and ordinarily resident in Hong Kong must register for a Hong Kong Identity Card.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Appointment availability at Registration of Persons Offices can be limited; booking within the first 2–3 days of arrival is advisable to guarantee a slot before the 30-day registration deadline. Walk-ins are generally not accepted.
non_obvious_action_required: Book online via the HKID appointment system immediately after arrival. Bring original passport with visa label, arrival stamp, and rental/employment contract for address verification.
source: Hong Kong Immigration Department – HKID Registration

step: Register for Hong Kong Identity Card (HKID) within 30 days of arrival
authority: Immigration Department – Registration of Persons Office
deadline_label: Within 30 days of arrival in Hong Kong
non_obvious_official_guidance: Failure to register for an HKID card within the prescribed period is a criminal offence under the Registration of Persons Ordinance (Cap. 177).
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 30-day clock runs from the date of arrival (not the date of visa grant). The HKID is a prerequisite for opening a Hong Kong bank account, signing a tenancy agreement, and registering with most government services. The card is collected 2–4 weeks after the registration appointment.
non_obvious_action_required: Attend the booked appointment with original passport, visa label, and a proof of address (employer letter or tenancy agreement). Biometric data (fingerprints and photo) will be captured. Plan for a gap of 2–4 weeks before the card can be collected; use the receipt as interim identification.
source: Hong Kong Immigration Department – Registration of Persons Ordinance (Cap. 177)

step: Employer enrols employee in a registered MPF scheme within 60 days of commencement of employment
deadline_label: Within 60 days of commencement of employment
non_obvious_official_guidance: An employer must enrol each eligible employee in a registered MPF scheme within 60 days of the employee's commencement of employment; failure is an offence under the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Ordinance (Cap. 485).
non_obvious_actual_reality: The first 60 days are an exemption period during which contributions are not yet required, but the enrolment itself should be set up well before day 60. Employer mandatory contributions are 5% of the employee's relevant income, capped at HKD 1,500 per month (income above HKD 30,000/month is not subject to mandatory contributions). A surcharge of 5–10% per annum applies to late contributions.
non_obvious_action_required: Select a registered MPF trustee from the MPFA-approved list; complete the trustee's enrolment form; notify the employee in writing of the chosen scheme and their right to make a separate Employee Choice Arrangement election for their own contribution portion.
source: MPFA – Employer Obligations under the MPF System

step: Employee elects preferred MPF scheme under the Employee Choice Arrangement (ECA)
deadline_label: Within 60 days of commencement of employment (align with employer enrolment)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under the Employee Choice Arrangement, employees may transfer their mandatory employee contributions to a registered MPF scheme of their own choice, separate from the employer's default scheme.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The ECA applies only to the employee's mandatory contribution portion; the employer's contributions must stay in the employer's chosen scheme until employment ends. An employee who intends to leave Hong Kong within a few years should select an ECA scheme with straightforward portability and fund withdrawal terms for non-permanent residents.
non_obvious_action_required: Employee selects a preferred registered MPF trustee independently of the employer, completes the trustee's transfer form, and notifies the employer's trustee. This election is portable across future HK employers.

step: Employer briefs employee on Hong Kong's territorial source basis for salaries tax
field_label: Salaries Tax – Territorial Source Principle Briefing
non_obvious_official_guidance: Salaries tax is charged on income arising in or derived from Hong Kong from any office or employment; income for services rendered wholly outside Hong Kong is not chargeable.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Only the portion of an employee's income attributable to days worked in Hong Kong is taxable; income earned for services rendered outside HK on business travel or remote work days may be excluded on a pro-rata days basis. Employers must track the employee's work-location split from day one — retrospective reconstruction is often rejected by the IRD.
non_obvious_action_required: Implement a travel/work-location diary for any employee spending material time outside Hong Kong on business. Retain records for at least 6 years. The apportionment claim is made on the employee's annual tax return and is subject to IRD scrutiny.

step: Explain that Hong Kong has no PAYE withholding; employee must self-budget for provisional salaries tax
field_label: Salaries Tax – No PAYE / Provisional Tax System
non_obvious_official_guidance: Salaries tax is assessed and collected after the year of assessment ends; the IRD issues provisional tax demand notes in advance based on estimated income.
non_obvious_actual_reality: There is no PAYE withholding in Hong Kong — the employer pays gross salary and the employee is solely responsible for paying tax on assessment. In the first year, the employee typically receives a combined demand for Year 1 confirmed tax plus Year 2 provisional tax simultaneously, creating a lump-sum payment often equivalent to roughly 18–30 months of tax liability in one bill. Employees accustomed to automatic withholding are frequently surprised by this.
non_obvious_action_required: Advise the employee to set aside approximately 15–17% of gross HK-source income each month in a separate account as a tax reserve. In the first year, the combined bill can arrive approximately 12–18 months after employment commences and must be paid in two instalments (typically January and April).

step: Employer files IR56E (notification of commencement of employment) with the Inland Revenue Department
deadline_label: Within 3 months of the employee's commencement of employment
non_obvious_official_guidance: An employer must notify the Commissioner of Inland Revenue within 3 months of an employee commencing employment; failure to do so is a criminal offence.
non_obvious_actual_reality: IR56E is a commencement-of-employment notice distinct from the annual IR56B return; many employers — especially those new to hiring in HK — overlook IR56E because they are focused on the annual return cycle. The IRD uses IR56E to open the employee's tax file proactively.
non_obvious_action_required: File IR56E via the IRD eTax portal (eTAX account required). Include: employee's full name, HKID number (or passport number if HKID not yet issued), correspondence address, commencement date, job title, and estimated annual remuneration. If the HKID number is not yet known at time of filing, file with passport details and submit a revised IR56E once HKID is obtained.
source: Inland Revenue Department – Employer's Return (IR56 Series)

step: Monitor 60-day visitor exemption applicability — confirm it does NOT apply to visa-holding employees
field_label: Salaries Tax – 60-Day Visitor Exemption (Inapplicable to Visa Holders)
deadline_label: Ongoing – assess per year of assessment (1 April – 31 March)
non_obvious_official_guidance: A person who renders services in Hong Kong for not more than 60 days in a year of assessment is exempt from salaries tax on income attributable to those services.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 60-day exemption applies only to genuine short-stay visitors — it ceases to apply once a person holds an HK employment visa or becomes ordinarily resident in HK. Employers sometimes incorrectly try to apply the 60-day rule to visa-holding secondees, which is not accepted by the IRD and creates a tax filing risk.
non_obvious_action_required: Do not attempt to structure a visa-holding employee's tax position around the 60-day visitor exemption. The correct framework for visa holders with split work locations is the pro-rata apportionment under the territorial source principle (see hk.salaries_tax.territorial_source_basis).
source: Inland Revenue Department – Salaries Tax – Exemptions

step: Track 183-day threshold where a Comprehensive Double Taxation Agreement (CDTA) may reduce HK salaries tax
deadline_label: Ongoing – assess per year of assessment; file claim on BIR60
non_obvious_official_guidance: Hong Kong has entered into Comprehensive Double Taxation Agreements (CDTAs) with approximately 45 jurisdictions; treaty relief may be available where an employee spends fewer than 183 days in Hong Kong in a 12-month period.
non_obvious_actual_reality: CDTA relief is not automatic; it must be claimed on the employee's HK salaries tax return (BIR60) and may also require a tax residence certificate from the home country's tax authority. The 183-day test and the reference period vary by treaty — some count calendar year, some the tax year, some any 12-month period. Additionally, the CDTA relief does not eliminate the underlying obligation to file in HK.
non_obvious_action_required: Track days in HK from day one. If the employee maintains genuine tax residence in their home country and splits time materially, engage a cross-border tax adviser to assess CDTA eligibility before year-end. Retain documentary evidence of home-country residence for at least 6 years.
source: Inland Revenue Department – Comprehensive Double Taxation Agreements

step: Employee files annual salaries tax return (BIR60) within the period stated on the notice
deadline_label: 1 month from date of issue (typically May – June each year; extensions available online)
source: Inland Revenue Department – Individual Tax Return (BIR60)

step: Employer files annual IR56B return (employer's return of remuneration and pensions) for each employee
field_label: IR56B – Annual Employer's Return of Remuneration
deadline_label: 1 month from date of issue (Employer's Return typically issued in April; due May)
non_obvious_official_guidance: An employer must report the total remuneration paid to each employee during the year of assessment, including salaries, commissions, bonuses, and benefits-in-kind.
non_obvious_actual_reality: IR56B must include all taxable benefits in kind: housing allowances, club memberships, school fees paid by employer, and — critically — equity remuneration (share awards, stock options) in the year of vesting or exercise, not the year of grant. Equity under-reporting is one of the most common IRD audit triggers for internationally mobile employees.
non_obvious_action_required: Obtain the equity vesting schedule and exercise history for the tax year from HR/share plan administrator; include the open-market value at vesting/exercise date. Employers with 10 or more employees must file electronically via eTax. Retain all IR56 filings and supporting schedules for at least 6 years.

step: Remit monthly MPF mandatory contributions by the contribution day each month
deadline_label: On or before the 10th of the calendar month following the contribution period
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employer and employee each contribute 5% of the employee's relevant income; contributions must be remitted to the MPF trustee by the contribution day (generally the 10th of the following month).
non_obvious_actual_reality: Mandatory contributions are capped: no contributions are required on monthly relevant income above HKD 30,000 (cap: HKD 1,500/month each side). Employees earning below HKD 7,100/month are not required to make employee contributions but the employer's 5% contribution still applies. A late-payment surcharge of 5–10% per annum applies automatically; the MPFA actively audits contribution records. MPF contributions may be withdrawn tax-free by non-permanent residents on permanent departure from HK.
non_obvious_action_required: Set up a direct debit or standing instruction with the MPF trustee to avoid inadvertent late payment. Confirm each month whether the contribution cap applies — do not over-withhold from high earners. Advise departing employees of their right to withdraw accrued MPF benefits upon permanent departure.

step: Apply to extend or renew the employment visa before it expires
deadline_label: Apply at least 6 weeks before visa expiry date
non_obvious_official_guidance: An employee whose limit of stay is about to expire must apply for an extension of stay before the expiry date; working after visa expiry is an offence.
non_obvious_actual_reality: GEP and ASMTP visas are typically granted for 1–2 years initially; the employer must re-sponsor each renewal. An employee may remain in HK and continue working during the processing period if they applied before expiry and can demonstrate the pending application (retain the acknowledgement receipt). TTPS holders must demonstrate continued employment or business activity to renew. Dependant visa renewals must be aligned with the principal's visa renewal timeline — a gap in the principal's visa automatically invalidates dependant status.
non_obvious_action_required: Diarise all visa expiry dates for the employee and dependants on the date of hire. For GEP/ASMTP, initiate the renewal process 6–8 weeks before expiry. For TTPS, prepare evidence of employment, income tax filing, and MPF contributions for the renewal application. Keep the acknowledgement receipt from the Immigration Department as proof of pending application.
source: Hong Kong Immigration Department – Extension of Stay
